Toppenish, in the Columbia River basin

01The workshop

Understanding a Climate of Change is a free, interactive workshop that runs in a web browser, built for school Chromebooks, and works offline once downloaded. Four questions guide it:

  1. 1How does a cloud work?
  2. 2How do you know what you know?
  3. 3What can we do?
  4. 4How do we work together?

Teachers and students follow air from the Pacific over the Cascades, see what river and weather gauges record, travel the salmon's journey home past the dams, sort climate actions by job, and watch a stress, and care, ripple through a web of relatives.

02How to use it

  • ←→NT

    Present it. Arrow keys move slides; N opens facilitator notes; T starts the clock.

  • 6 to 12

    Teach from it. Every part has matching hands-on lessons for Grades 6 to 12.

  • offline

    Take it offline. Download the project from GitHub and open docs/index.html.

With gratitude to the Yakama Nation, whose homelands, waters, and people host this gathering.

03What's inside

The four units follow the same parts, so you can walk from the workshop into your classroom with one structure. An opening and a closing lesson hold them together, the way a circle holds a conversation.
